reference: Native CPython 3.14 with pydantic-ai-slim 2.60.0 and pydantic-graph 2.60.0
requestReference: pydantic_ai.models.openai.OpenAIChatModel._map_messages and _map_tool_definition; the hash-pinned openai SDK is CPython dev-only
normalizations: Assistant tool-only content null maps to the bridge's empty string.
LangChain message roles and tool calls map back to OpenAI-format request messages; tool-call IDs and JSON argument strings remain compared.
Reply transcripts project text and tool calls without provider-generated message IDs or timestamps.
Native cancellation and the runtime's cancelled event share the fixed cancelled code and message.
Text chunks follow the scripted word boundaries, and stream envelopes omit runtime-generated run/event IDs.
Streamed tool arguments compare as normalized JSON because the JavaScript provider serializes its parsed final arguments.

Both streaming projections use agent.iter so model-request markers correspond to actual request nodes; this uses the same node streaming API as run_stream_events without its background convenience task.
limits: A route without the tool-calling feature fails unavailable under the existing router semantics; a leased model without bindTools fails unsupported. Both fail before provider dispatch, without fallback.
All model replies are deterministic scripts. Native conformance blocks socket connections; Pyodide fixtures block external requests and use verified local assets.
The capability-denial fixture raises the same fixed denial from a native tool and the JavaScript broker binding.
The argument-block fixture applies a native fixed-denial stand-in; the Pyodide lanes prove the JavaScript output-safety check blocks the arguments before Python receives them.
The stream-id-block and stream-mid-block fixtures apply native fixed-denial stand-ins; the Pyodide lanes exercise JavaScript checks before forwarding the blocked fragment.
The final-mismatch fixture corrupts only the checked final bridge content in the Pyodide lanes; the native scripted stream emits the same fixed invalid outcome after its text deltas.
The stream-abort native fixture cancels after the first text chunk; Pyodide lanes cancel the runtime after the first host message event.
Approvals, durable conversations, reload behavior and real-model quality remain unclaimed.
